items.originalTitle: The Federal Reserve's Latest October Inflation Forecast Has Arrived, and It's Terrible News for Wall Street
items.originalSummary: Year four of Wall Street's bull market didn't disappoint. The artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure build-out lifted the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI), S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC), and Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) to several record highs throughout 2026. But expecting the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite to head higher amid persistently elevated inflation is a tall task. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) have quite the challenge on their hands in delivering price stability . Unfortunately, the latest inflation update for October hasn't done policymakers or Wall Street any favors. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

items.title: 馬斯克公開支持 SpaceX 與特斯拉的交易可能會為談判帶來麻煩
items.originalTitle: Musk’s public endorsement of SpaceX-Tesla deal may throw a wrench in talks By Reuters
items.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s public endorsement this week of a potential $3.5 trillion merger between SpaceX and Tesla has rattled some insiders involved in the discussions, who worry his comments could invite shareholder scrutiny and delay the process by several weeks, according to a person with direct knowledge of the talks.The disclosure created a ”mess” for the process, as it could lead to questions about how well Tesla shareholders’ interests would be represented, the person said. The concerns reflect similarities some participants see with Tesla’s 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, which sparked years of litigation over Musk’s role in the deal.Musk, who serves as CEO of both SpaceX and Tesla and owns significant stakes in each company, this week told investors that the two companies were examining what would be the largest corporate transaction in history and revealed that both had formed special committees to evaluate it. The backlash to those remarks is reported here for the first time.The parties have hired advisers, but discussions are at an early stage, three sources familiar with the matter said. SpaceX approached Tesla in recent weeks, and the companies have been discussing a range of transaction structures, including a SpaceX acquisition of Tesla or a merger under a newly formed holding company, the person familiar with the matter said. They are weighing different forms of merger consideration, including an all-stock deal, the person said. These details of the talks have not been previously reported.Tesla, SpaceX and Musk did not respond to requests for comment. Shareholder litigation over Tesla's SolarCity deal In related-party transactions such as a SpaceX-Tesla merger, independent board members typically oversee the process to safeguard public shareholders’ interests.That issue loomed large in Tesla’s 2016 acquisition of SolarCity, which triggered years of litigation after shareholders alleged the world’s richest man had influenced the process to bail out his investment in the struggling rooftop solar company. At the time, Musk owned roughly 22% of both Tesla and SolarCity, which was founded by his cousins.Shareholders argued that Musk’s involvement and public support undermined the deal’s fairness. Central to the case were claims that despite his minority stake, Musk was a controlling shareholder of Tesla due to his ties to board members and domineering style.The Delaware Supreme Court later noted that plaintiffs’ contention of the absence of an independent committee, together with ”certain other facts concerning Musk’s involvement in and public support for the transaction,” warranted the finding of unfair dealing.The courts ultimately upheld the acquisition as fair, though it took several years for the case to be resolved and Tesla directors settled allegations for $60 million. items.title: 納斯達克、國債殖利率和美元面臨人工智慧情緒的重大考驗
items.originalTitle: Nasdaq, Treasury yields and dollar face a major AI sentiment test
items.originalSummary: Asian technology shares fell on Tuesday as investors assessed fresh pressure on the artificial intelligence trade ahead of major US corporate earnings. South Korea’s Kospi Index dropped 3.9%, while chipmaker SK Hynix headed toward its lowest closing level since April. The MSCI Asia Pacific Index lost 1.4%, reversing the direction of Monday’s technology-led gains on Wall Street. Nasdaq 100 futures also weakened, and the dollar slipped against major currencies as traders weighed higher financing costs and rising oil prices.Bloomberg reported that the pullback followed a brief US technology recovery that failed to lift the wider stock market. Upcoming results from major companies now offer a test of investor confidence in AI spending and the demand supporting semiconductor shares..South Korean Chip Shares Lead Asian Market Decline.South Korea bore the sharpest losses as chip shares extended their retreat. The local market serves as a key gauge of investor appetite for companies linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure. At the same time, data-center company Elice plunged as much as 33% during its Seoul trading debut.Elsewhere, Japan’s Topix fell 1.5%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined 1.2%, and the Shanghai Composite lost 0.6%. The MSCI Emerging Markets Index also dropped 1.2%, while Euro Stoxx 50 futures indicated a 0.7% decline at the European open.The broad regional weakness contrasted with Monday’s US trading. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 1.6%, ending an eight-session losing streak, its longest since 2008. The advance helped the Nasdaq 100 recover after its weakest week since April 2025’s tariff-related turmoil.Still, the recovery remained concentrated in technology. Roughly 65% of S&P 500 members finished Monday lower, according to the market report. That imbalance showed how gains among a small group of stocks differed from conditions across the wider market..AI Earnings Face Scrutiny as Funding Costs Rise.Investors now face several earnings announcements that could reshape expectations for technology companies. Netflix reports Tuesday, followed Wednesday by Tesla, Meta Platforms and IBM. Their updates arrive after heavy AI spending and rising borrowing costs unsettled technology shares.Can the coming earnings reports sustain confidence in the AI investment boom? The question follows fresh concern about financing large computing projects. In Asia, SoftBank’s credit-default swap spreads rose to their highest level in nearly four years amid funding concerns and talk of a major acquisition.Meanwhile, Nscale entered talks over a reported USD 45 billion computing arrangement with Anthropic. The discussions showed the scale of proposed infrastructure commitments even as investors reassessed borrowing costs and the financial outlook for AI-related businesses.Treasury markets reflected that pressure. The US 10-year yield eased two basis points to 5.12% after Monday’s rise, when reduced demand for safer assets pushed yields higher. Japan’s 10-year yield climbed to 2.920%, while Australia’s advanced to 5.25%.Also Read: AI-Driven Cyber Threats Put Asian Banks, Businesses on High Alert.Oil Prices and Currency Moves Add Market Pressu

items.originalSummary: Bitcoin climbed to around $84,500, marking a weekly high.On Oct. 21, blockchain media outlet Decrypt reported that bitcoin was trading around $84,500, up 2.5 percent over 24 hours. It said the cryptocurrency market capitalisation rose 2.2 percent to $2.9 trillion.Altcoins also rose. Ether gained 2.5 percent to $2,504, Solana rose 2.2 percent to $108.18, and BNB added 2 percent to $749. Among major tokens, XRP rose 4.1 percent to $1.37, while Zcash (ZEC) surged 11.2 percent to around $1,332.Overall market sentiment also eased somewhat. The crypto Fear and Greed Index rose 3 points from the previous day to 55, staying in the neutral zone. This is interpreted as a signal that investors have moved out of panic but have not yet begun actively buying.The macro environment also eased some of the burden. Brent crude moved between $97 and $112 a barrel this month before trading near $108 on the day, and the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield also calmed somewhat. Rising oil prices stoke inflation worries, and price pressures then push Treasury yields higher again, tightening funding for risk assets.Still, the interest-rate variable remains. The Federal Reserve's policy rate has held at 3.75 to 4 percent since a September hike. The market sees a high chance of a hold at the Oct. 28 meeting, but is pricing in a higher likelihood of an additional hike on Dec. 9. That has made it important whether this rebound leads to a trend reversal or remains a technical bounce under rate pressure.Technically, regaining the $81,603 support level is key. Bitcoin fell below that level during an October pullback and then recovered it. The 50-day exponential moving average is around $80,782, and the 200-day exponential moving average is near $76,084. The relative strength index (RSI) stands at 58.5, favouring buyers but not in overbought territory.In the near term, the key is whether it breaks above $84,726. If bitcoin forms a daily close above that level, $86,090 and the September high of $87,422.70 were presented as the next target zone. If it slips below $81,603, $80,782, $79,711 and $76,084 are cited in order as lower support levels. On prediction market Myriad, the probability of bitcoin reaching $87,500 within October was reflected at 31 percent, and the probability of reaching $90,000 at 18 percent.This rebound is drawing attention because it confirms not only a price rise but also the recovery of the $81,603 support level and outperformance versus key moving averages. Still, with oil and interest-rate pressure remaining, further confirmation is needed on whether a technical rebound will turn into a trend reversal.

items.originalSummary: Google's first orbital AI test carries four chips and runs on about as much power as a hair dryer. James Altucher points to a much bigger plan: the million-satellite fleet Musk has on file with federal regulators. Washington, D.C., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Google put AI in space on October 1. It needed Elon Musk to get there. Google's Project Suncatcher test satellite is about the size of a refrigerator. It carries four of Google's AI chips. And it reached orbit on a SpaceX Falcon 9, sharing the ride with other payloads.

historyItems.originalTitle: IBM Stock Rises After-Hours, Tops Q3 Revenue Estimates On Software Strength And Recovery In Delayed Contracts
historyItems.originalSummary: International Business Machines Corporation IBM reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings rising 11% year over year to $2.95 per share. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.88 by 2.4%. Revenues increased 4.7% to $17.10 billion, surpassing the consensus mark of $16.87 billion by 1.4%. The upside reflected accelerating Software and Infrastructure growth, improved transaction execution and productivity initiatives. Software annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $24.9 billion, up 8% year over year. Operating pre-tax margin expanded 70 basis points (bps).

historyItems.title: LRCX：創紀錄的收入和收益，12 月季度指引收入為 $8.60B
historyItems.summary: 營收：82.2億美元，季增22%，年增54%；連續第五個季度營收創紀錄。毛利率：由於良好的客戶和產品組合，達到創紀錄的 52.4%，高於 6 月季度的 52%。營業利益率：創紀錄的 40.2%，高於 6 月季度的 38.4%；首次突破40%。稀釋後每股盈餘：創紀錄的 2.20 美元；稀釋後股數約12.6億。
historyItems.originalTitle: LRCX: Record revenue and earnings, with December-quarter guidance for $8.60B revenue
historyItems.originalSummary: Revenue: $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% year-over-year; fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue. Gross Margin: Record 52.4%, up from 52% in the June quarter on favorable customer and product mix. Operating Margin: Record 40.2%, up from 38.4% in the June quarter; first time topping 40%. Diluted EPS: Record $2.20; diluted share count ~1.26 billion. Operating Expenses: $1 billion, up from $916 million prior quarter; R&D ~two-thirds of total. Deferred Revenue: $2.66 billion, up $227 million from the June quarter. Memory Systems Revenue: 46% of systems revenue (record dollar level), up 120% year-over-year; NAND 26% of systems revenue (up from 23%), NAND dollars up ~40% sequentially; DRAM 20% of systems revenue (down from 23%), record dollar level. Foundry Systems Revenue: Record; 46% of systems revenue, up from 44% in the June quarter. Logic and Other Systems Revenue: 8% of systems revenue, down from 10% in the June quarter. CSBG Revenue: Fourth consecutive record quarter at nearly $2.5 billion, up slightly sequentially and 40% year-over-year; calendar 2026 growth expected above 30% year-over-year, with over 15% growth expected in calendar 2027.

historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together . Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes." The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.

investorBrief.event: 馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 花了數年時間將特斯拉和 SpaceX 打造成兩個價值數萬億美元的科技帝國。現在，他正在考慮讓他們在一起。週二被問及合併是否是一個好主意時，馬斯克明確表示：「是的。」前景不僅僅是假設。馬斯克表示，已經成立了特別委員會來評估潛在的交易，但他強調，不能保證合併一定會發生，也沒有達成任何協議。

historyItems.originalTitle: Tesla and SpaceX Formed Committees to Discuss Potential Merger, Elon Musk Says
historyItems.originalSummary: Wall Street is sounding bullish on SpaceX ahead of its third-quarter earnings report, to be delivered after the bell on Tuesday. Mizuho has an outperform rating on the stock and a $200 price target, per a Monday note from analyst Brett Linzey. Shares were trading around $148 as of 10:45 a.m. on Tuesday. "AI is the largest swing factor for 3Q26 revenue and EBITDA. Consensus has AI revenue of $6.30B (+146% Q/Q from $2.56B) and AI adj. EBITDA of $3.32B (from $1.15B)," he wrote. Analysts are expecting some conversation about deals or competitive plays with cable and telecom companies following SpaceX's acquisition of low-band spectrum earlier this month. "We expect initial strategic commentary centers around Connectivity and how SPCX can partner/compete its way into global markets, although we think low-band distribution becomes a meaningful intelligence lever over time," Colin Canfield at Cantor Fitzgerald wrote in a Monday note. He has a price target of $246 and an overweight rating on the stock. Oppenheimer's expectations are more measured. The bank thinks the quarter will be "in-line" with "guidance reiterated." "Industry subscriber growth is slowing with limited room for pricing action, so focus is shifting from net adds and service revenue growth toward cost-cutting using AI, and lower subsidies/churn," Timothy Horan at Oppenheimer told clients in a Tuesday note. He expects "more rational incumbent behavior" from SpaceX's competitors. –Tobias Burns

historyItems.originalTitle: Space X and Tesla exploring merger, CEO Elon Musk says
historyItems.originalSummary: It's official: Tesla and SpaceX are in talks. Independent board members at the two Elon Musk-led companies have formed special committees to hash over a possible merger, Musk told investors during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call Tuesday. "These special committees consist of independent directors, and because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," said Musk, who was asked about a potential combination during the call. "This is definitely the kind of question where I feel like I'm tap dancing through a minefield."

historyItems.summary: （彭博）—波音公司的 737 Max 10 噴射機獲得了美國監管機構的批准，結束了該飛機製造商窄體飛機系列漫長的認證傳奇，該系列飛機因兩起致命事故和一系列品質缺陷而中斷。 737 Max 10 是該公司最大的單通道飛機，是波音對競爭對手空中巴士 SE 的 A321neo 的回應。該飛機的訂單量超過 1,500 架，使其成為最受歡迎的 Max 機型之一，由聯合航空控股公司 (United Airlines Holdings Inc.) 和阿拉斯加航空集團公司 (Alaska Air Group Inc.) 等美國航空公司購買。
historyItems.originalTitle: Boeing wins FAA approval for 737 Max 10 after years of delays as Duffy says certification process should be faster
historyItems.originalSummary: (Bloomberg) -- Boeing Co. won US regulator approval for its 737 Max 10 jet, capping off a lengthy certification saga for the planemaker’s family of narrowbody aircraft that was disrupted by two fatal crashes and a series of quality lapses.The 737 Max 10 is the largest of the company’s single-aisle aircraft and is Boeing’s response to rival Airbus SE’s A321neo. The plane’s 1,500-plus order book makes it one of the more popular Max variants, purchased by US carriers like United Airlines Holdings Inc. and Alaska Air Group Inc. The Max 10’s smallest sibling, the 737 Max 7, was approved by the US Federal Aviation Administration in August.“The FAA’s decision follows a thorough review of the aircraft’s design and safety requirements,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said in a news release, adding that the regulator will “continue to hold Boeing to the highest safety standards” moving forward.Bloomberg reported in July that the FAA was expected to certify the Max 10 around October. The timeline was briefly in doubt after the planemaker disclosed a software glitch with the airplane’s navigation system, but an FAA panel determined the issue did not pose a safety risk.“The 737-10 offers greater capacity, longer range and the best seat economics in its class, a platform that will create more value and opportunities for airlines around the world,” Boeing Commercial Airplanes Chief Executive Officer Stephanie Pope said in a statement Tuesday.The Max 10 is one of Boeing’s most important new jets, offering airlines a solution to replace the out-of-production 757. Alongside the other Max models, the largest variant will help the planemaker repair its balance sheet and pare down debt. The aircraft can seat as many as 230 passengers and fly for up to 3,100 nautical miles, according to Boeing’s website.US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said streamlining aircraft certification is essential to America’s ability to compete with Europe and China, noting that it took nearly a decade to approve the Max 10. “I have to allow you all to certify ​aircraft faster,” Duffy told a ceremony at Boeing’s widebody site north of Seattle on Tuesday. “You have to come to the market more quickly.”Regulators in Canada and Europe are expected to complete their own Max 10 approvals in “probably a couple months,” Mike Sinnett, a Boeing executive over development programs, said later.

historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile Advances Service Readiness Ahead of Initial Space-Based Cellular Broadband Coverage in Key Global Markets
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile, Inc. announced it is advancing service readiness in key global markets before the end of 2026, including the United States, Canada, Japan, United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia. AST SpaceMobile now has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed, or in planning worldwide. The expansive ground network supports AST SpaceMobile?s global commercial ecosystem with over 60 mobile network operators who cover over 3 billion subscribers, bringing a third layer of connectivity directly into the mobile networks people already use.Spectrum is a key component of this readiness. AST SpaceMobile combines strategic partner operators? spectrum with access to mobile satellite services (MSS) spectrum, targeting approximately 100 MHz of access in the United States.Its spectrum position includes access to 45 MHz of MSS mid-band spectrum in North America and priority rights to 60 MHz of S-band spectrum globally on a market-by-market basis. The company?s satellite technology can tune across approximately 1,150 MHz of low- and mid-band frequencies globally, providing flexibility to serve different markets using available partner and satellite spectrum, subject to applicable regulatory approvals. Supporting this service rollout, AST SpaceMobile?s ground network connects the company?s growing satellite constellation with mobile operators?core networks, routing voice, video and broadband data between space and ground-based infrastructure, making it a key component of the end-to-end infrastructure required to deliver space-based cellular broadband connectivity through partners to people everywhere they work, live, and travel. This integration enables operators to extend their reach beyond the limits of terrestrial coverage while evolving alongside future 3GPP standards. In the United States, the Company has already enabled over 3,000 coverage cells and expects to activate the roughly 5,600 cellular cells that cover the continuous United States before year-end.Enabling the remaining digital cells will establish the geographic footprint required to support initial, intermittent service across the contiguous United States and is a prerequisite for nationwide rollout. During this initial phase, service will be available within the satellites? coverage area.Additional spacecraft deployments will extend the duration and frequency of coverage as AST SpaceMobile advances toward continuous service. BlueBird satellites are assembled, integrated, and tested at AST SpaceMobile?s facilities in Midland, Texas, with production now progressing through BlueBird 50. Service availability will expand as satellite capacity and ground infrastructure are deployed and network integration progresses, subject to applicable authorizations.

historyItems.summary: Arista Networks 最近推出了開放式乙太網路機架規模產品組合，包括 Etherlink SU-144 架構，以支援高密度 AI 基礎設施，每個機架最多有 144 個加速器，並採用專為極端功耗和散熱需求量身定制的液冷設計。基於 ESUN 的平台和 Netdi 基金會旨在為雲端和 AI 營運商提供一種開放的、以標準為中心的專有互連替代方案，將 Arista 的硬體與 Neocloud 按代幣成本優先級和多供應商 AI 計算生態系統緊密聯繫起來。這項發展也塑造了 Arista Networks 更廣泛的投資敘述，重點是 Etherlink SU-144 AI 機架規模擴展。
historyItems.originalTitle: Is Open AI Rack Launch Altering The Investment Case For Arista Networks Stock?
historyItems.originalSummary: Arista Networks recently launched an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, including the Etherlink SU-144 architecture, to support high-density AI infrastructure with up to 144 accelerators per rack and liquid-cooled designs tailored for extreme power and thermal demands. The ESUN-based platforms and Netdi foundation aim to give cloud and AI operators an open, standards-focused alternative to proprietary interconnects, linking Arista's hardware closely to neocloud cost-per-token priorities and multi-vendor AI compute ecosystems. This development also shapes Arista Networks' broader investment narrative, with a focus on the Etherlink SU-144 AI rack-scale expansion.

historyItems.originalTitle: GE Vernova secures order aimed to strengthen regional energy capacity in Côte d’Ivoire
historyItems.originalSummary: Developed by Songon Energies S.A., Songon power plant is built to strengthen energy security and support future growing electricity demand in Greater Abidjan GE Vernova 9E turbine technology to support reliable power delivery for industrial growth and millions of households Infrastructure development expected to create up to 1,400 new jobs and drive positive community impact ABIDJAN, Côte d'Ivoire - [October 20, 2026] - GE Vernova announced today that it will provide the gas power technology forthe new Songon combined-cycle power plant, located in the Songon region near Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. Following the signing of financing agreements last June, Songon Energies- Ivorian development investment company focused on advancing energy infrastructure - selected GE Vernova to supply a 9E gas turbine and generator. The plant - to be built by the EPC contractor China Energy International Engineering Co., Ltd. - is expected to deliver 372 megawatts (MW), a capacity equal to the power needs of approximately 5 million Ivorian homes. Supporting a growing national energy landscape. Côte d'Ivoire has made significant progress, reaching an electrification rate of 94.3 percent by 2024 through initiatives like the "Electricity for All Program" (PEPT), in line with the national goal to achieve universal electrification and improved power quality by 2030. Despite these gains, the nation faces an annual demand growth rate of 10 to 15 percent and rural areas still require expanded access. In this energy landscape, this new power plant will help fill a critical gap. The facility is projected to represent up to 12 percent of the country's total installed base upon its scheduled 2029 operational launch, playing a vital role in meeting these ambitious development targets. Furthermore, the project is expected to generate up to 1,400 new jobs, creating economic opportunities for the local community. "The Songon Energies project is designed to strengthen energy security and support future growing electricity demand growth in the Greater Abidjan region while reinforcing the country's position as a regional energy hub in West Africa," said Mr. Wang Xiaoming, Deputy General Manager (Acting CEO) for Songon Energies. "The facility is expected to ease energy pressure on the Abidjan metropolitan area, providing a reliable foundation for the development of skilled workers, the growth of industrial zones, the expansion of small and medium-sized enterprises, and a tangible improvement in the daily lives of millions of Ivorian households. We selected to work with GE Vernova for this new power plant, because of our deep trust in their efficient technology and their constant, proven presence in Côte d'Ivoire, which gives us great confidence in the long-term success of this facility." "We are honored to support Songon Energies with our proven 9E technology for this crucial infrastructure project," said Joseph Anis, CEO of Gas Power in Europe, Middle East, and Africa at GE Vernova. historyItems.originalTitle: Vishay Intertechnology (VSH) Launches New Sensors, Is It Still A Bargain?
historyItems.originalSummary: Highlights Vishay Intertechnology introduced automotive-grade optical sensors for battery management, energy storage and industrial automation applications. The sensors support high-speed, wear-free optical communication with electromagnetic interference immunity. The product launch expands the company's component offerings for electric vehicles, industrial equipment and other specialised electronic systems. Vishay Intertechnology (NYSE:VSH) operates in the semiconductor and electronic components sector, supplying products used in automotive systems, industrial equipment, computing hardware and other electronic applications. The company announced a new range of automotive-grade optical sensors designed for battery management, energy storage and industrial automation systems. The launch expands the company's offerings for applications that require reliable data communication in electrically demanding environments. Optical sensors can support communication between electronic components while reducing dependence on conventional electrical signalling in suitable system designs. The products are intended for applications where electromagnetic interference, operational reliability and communication integrity are important engineering considerations. Electric vehicles and automated manufacturing equipment contain multiple electronic subsystems that exchange information to monitor operating conditions and coordinate functions. Optical Sensors and High-Speed Communication The newly introduced sensors support high-speed, wear-free optical data communication. Optical communication uses light to transmit information, offering an alternative to electrical signalling in applications where electrical noise can affect signal integrity. Electromagnetic interference can arise from motors, switching circuits, power electronics and other electrical equipment. In electric vehicles, battery systems and power conversion hardware operate alongside control electronics, creating demanding conditions for signal transmission. Optical communication can help address some of these challenges by reducing susceptibility to electromagnetic interference along the optical communication path. The practical benefits depend on system architecture, component integration and the requirements of the application. The sensors are designed for mission-critical hardware environments, where dependable communication supports monitoring and control functions. Their wear-free communication approach also addresses applications in which contact-based transmission methods may introduce mechanical limitations. The product announcement identifies electromagnetic immunity and cybersecurity resilience as relevant design features. These characteristics align with the requirements of modern electronic systems, although actual system-level protection depends on implementation, software, network architecture and other safeguards. historyItems.originalTitle: AstraZeneca and Oracle launch global AI collaboration to advance clinical trial optimisation and support better patient outcomes
historyItems.originalSummary: Partnership aims to advance solutions to improve care pathways, clinical trial matching, safety monitoring, and guideline-directed care AstraZeneca and Oracle Health and Life Sciences today announced a unique collaboration to leverage AstraZeneca's scientific, clinical development and regulatory expertise with Oracle's real-world data, cloud infrastructure, and AI-enabled clinical capabilities to accelerate clinical research and bring evidence-driven insights into care workflows to accelerate clinical trial optimisation and help more patients receive the right care sooner. Many serious conditions are diagnosed late; patients can wait a long time before they are referred and there are gaps in how we translate scientific advancements into clinical practice. This collaboration is designed to test practical ways to connect scientific research directly to clinical workflows and transform care. Initial areas of exploration include clinical trial recruitment, earlier diagnosis, drug-safety monitoring and leveraging real-world evidence across the lifecycle of a medicine. Programmes will span AstraZeneca's core disease areas including oncology, cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases, respiratory and immunology, and rare disease. The collaboration will span multiple international projects with key regions including the US, Middle East, and Europe working with local governments and within applicable regulations to ensure these could be scaled in the future. The first programme will focus on supporting hypertension care and clinical research in Abu Dhabi, in partnership with healthcare company, M42. This will help clinical teams identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension; implementing guideline-directed care; and improving the recruitment for clinical trials. Pascal Soriot, Chief Executive Officer, AstraZeneca said: "This unique collaboration brings leaders in healthcare and AI together at a global scale to accelerate the journey from the discovery of medicine to patient care. Combining AstraZeneca's world class science with Oracle's deep data and technology expertise, we can help clinicians identify patients sooner, optimise clinical trials, and generate evidence continuously across the lifecycle of a medicine." Mike Sicilia, chief executive officer, Oracle said: "Some of the most important opportunities for AI are in healthcare, where better use of data can help turn scientific innovation into better outcomes for patients. By bringing AstraZeneca's scientific expertise together with Oracle's data, cloud, AI, and healthcare capabilities, we have an opportunity to help accelerate research, connect more patients to clinical trials, and ultimately bring relevant insights into care faster." Anne-Claire Gerbaldi, Chief Digital, Data and AI Officer, AstraZeneca, said: "Too many patients are diagnosed late or face a long journey to get the care they need. historyItems.summary: Super Micro Computer（納斯達克GS：SMCI）宣布推出基於開放運算專案的全新人工智慧和高效能運算資料中心解決方案，目標是機架規模部署。擴展後的 OCP 認可產品組合現已涵蓋用於節能、密集 AI 叢集的系統、機架、液體冷卻設備和網路硬體。該公司任命 Mark Long 為財務官，增加了西部數據和其他大型科技集團的高階主管財務經驗。基於 OCP 的人工智慧和 HPC 的推出，加上聘請 Mark Long 擔任財務官，與我們的研究標記的更廣泛的主題相一致。
historyItems.originalTitle: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) Unveils OCP AI Systems And Names Mark Long CFO
historyItems.originalSummary: Super Micro Computer (NasdaqGS:SMCI) announced new Open Compute Project based AI and high performance computing data center solutions targeting rack scale deployments. The expanded OCP Accepted portfolio now covers systems, racks, liquid cooling gear, and networking hardware for energy efficient, dense AI clusters. The company named Mark Long as Chief Financial Officer, adding executive finance experience from Western Digital and other large tech groups. The OCP based AI and HPC rollout plus the hiring of Mark Long as CFO comes alongside wider themes our research has flagged. Our analysis turns up 2 warning signs (1 major) for Super Micro Computer as well. For readers tracking the build out of AI data center infrastructure, it is worth comparing Super Micro Computer with other hardware and tooling suppliers through 55 AI infrastructure stocks .

historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile launch schedule updated
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile and TELUS completed an integration test linking TELUS' terrestrial wireless network with AST SpaceMobile's space based system, aiming to extend direct satellite connectivity for Canadian smartphone users in remote and underserved areas. The push into satellite to phone service comes as AST SpaceMobile faces launch schedule uncertainty and rising competitive pressure from SpaceX in both spectrum access and satellite deployment. This article examines how AST SpaceMobile's investment narrative is affected by launch delays and intensifying SpaceX competition in satellite connectivity.

historyItems.summary: 人工智慧雲端供應商 CoreWeave Inc.（CRWV，金融）正成為投資者為人工智慧熱潮提供資金支持程度的測試案例。該公司 6 月發行的債券殖利率為 9.675%，但目前已大幅下跌，殖利率高達 15% 左右。
historyItems.originalTitle: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
historyItems.originalSummary: CoreWeave Inc. ( CRWV , Financials ), an AI cloud provider, is becoming a test case of how far investors would go to fund the AI boom.The company's bonds, issued in June at a yield of 9.675%, have plummeted so much that yields are up to around 15%. That's more important than another terrible day for the stock.Credit investors are asking if the cash future data-centre projects will earn will arrive fast enough to support the debt incurred today.The argument is about CoreWeave, which depends significantly on external financing to finance its expansion.Investors are also beginning to look closely at leverage, collateral and the chance that pricey GPUs might become obsolete before certain facilities are up and running.The wider conclusion is that it could be tougher and more expensive to support AI infrastructure.Dan Ives puts the figure of planned projects that may never be constructed at 5% to 10%.That doesn't imply the AI buildout is done, though. It does indicate capital is getting less forgiving.The next thing to monitor is whether CoreWeave bond yields stabilize, since sustained stress might change the price and availability of loans throughout the larger AI infrastructure market.

historyItems.originalTitle: Test: The 2026 Ford F-150 STX Lobo Fails to Impress for the Money
historyItems.originalSummary: Ford makes the long haul and enters Grasso’s Garage with an aesthetically pleasing and proven F-150 Lobo edition pickup truck that is ready for all consumers. With a 600-mile range on a full tank, our F-150 Lobo tester offers an upgraded 5.0-liter Coyote V-8 engine packed with 400 horsepower and 410 lb.-ft. of torque. Paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission, the F-150 Lobo gets up and goes and is smooth. Wrapped in Oxford White, the Lobo package is an additional $4,695 and includes 22-inch gloss black wheels, an electronic locking rear axle and all-season tires. Our STX Series pickup comes with LED fog lights, black cloth interior and a black and dark gray grill. Upgraded options include a tray style floor liner, mobile office package, 36-gallon fuel tank, SiriusXM and spray-in bedliner for a combined additional $2,630 total. While the interior is simple and typical Ford, it serves the consumers well with its 12-inch SYNC4 infotainment system. Rear-view camera and parking sensors, selectable drive modes and a host of safety features came standard on our weeklong tester. Standard warranty is a 3-year / 36,000 mile bumper to bumper, a 5-year / 60,000 mile powertrain, and a 5-year / 60,000 mile roadside assistance.

historyItems.originalTitle: Prediction market odds on Tesla-SpaceX merger are above 50% for early 2027
historyItems.originalSummary: The prediction market odds of a merger between Tesla and SpaceX have risen above 50% for early 2027, according to CNBC. This increase reflects heightened speculation around a possible union of the two companies, both controlled by Elon Musk. Notably, these odds do not stem from any formal announcement or filing, but rather from market activity and sentiment. Recent analyses, including one from Barclays, suggest potential scenarios for a merger, though official confirmations from either company remain absent. Observers should monitor communications from Tesla and SpaceX, particularly any formal disclosures or statements from Elon Musk. An SEC filing or official press release could significantly impact current market pricing. Additionally, regulatory reviews or statements from antitrust authorities may influence the perceived likelihood of a merger. As market participants react to new information, shifts in pricing could further indicate changing expectations.

historyItems.summary: Arista Networks (ANET) 透過新的開放式乙太網路機架規模產品組合將高密度人工智慧基礎設施置於其故事的中心，旨在跨液冷機架連接加速器以處理大規模工作負載。最新的人工智慧機架規模發布是在 Arista Networks 股價強勁上漲後推出的，該股 90 天股價回報率上漲 15.51%，今年迄今上漲 57.84%，而五年內的長期股東總回報率約為 8 倍。截至最後收盤價 210.88 美元，1 天股價回報率下跌 2.70％，儘管 30 天漲幅 5.66％ 和 1 年股東總回報率 43.02％ 表明持續的勢頭，受到先前對 Arista 800G 交換產品的興趣以及對人工智能基礎設施需求日益關注的支持。
historyItems.originalTitle: Arista Networks (ANET) Stock Forecast and Price Target 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: Arista Networks (ANET) has put high-density AI infrastructure at the center of its story with a new open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, aiming to link accelerators across liquid-cooled racks for large-scale workloads. The latest AI rack-scale launch lands after a strong run in Arista Networks' shares, with the stock up 15.51% on a 90-day share price return and 57.84% year to date, while long-term total shareholder return over five years is about 8x. At a last close of US$210.88, the 1-day share price return fell 2.70% even as the 30-day gain of 5.66% and 1-year total shareholder return of 43.02% indicate ongoing momentum, supported by prior interest in Arista's 800G switching products and growing attention on AI infrastructure demand.

historyItems.originalTitle: Taiwan chipmaker TSMC explores Texas investment to expand production in the US
historyItems.originalSummary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), the world’s largest contract chipmaker, is exploring an expansion into Texas as demand for artificial intelligence chips continues to surge. The company confirmed that it had sent teams to Texas to assess potential investment opportunities. Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei said TSMC was evaluating options to expand its U.S. manufacturing footprint beyond Arizona. “The demand, actually, is still far above our capability today to supply, and we’re working very hard to narrow the gap,” Wei said . READ: Nvidia in talks to acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion (August 27, 2026) The potential Texas investment would be in addition to TSMC’s existing commitment of $265 billion to expand semiconductor manufacturing in the United States, including facilities in Arizona. In July, the company announced an additional $100 billion investment , bringing its total planned U.S. investment to $265 billion. Wei said the investment would help expand the U.S. semiconductor industry, strengthen supply chain resilience and create well-paying jobs in the high-tech sector. TSMC is also discussing a possible role in Elon Musk’s proposed Terafab chip manufacturing complex in Texas. Musk has promoted the project as a way to increase chip production for his businesses, including SpaceX and Tesla. Wei said any factory operated by TSMC would have to remain under the Taiwanese company’s control. Musk, however, has said his companies would build and operate the facility, with TSMC potentially leasing part of it. The companies have not announced a final agreement. TSMC manufactures more than 90% of the world’s most advanced chips and supplies major technology companies, including Apple and Nvidia. As the AI industry’s computing needs grow, semiconductor manufacturers are under increasing pressure to expand production and meet demand. The company’s latest financial results reflect the surge in demand. TSMC reported net profit of 763.1 billion New Taiwan dollars, or about $24 billion, for the July-September quarter, a 69% increase from a year earlier. Revenue rose 51% to 1.49 trillion New Taiwan dollars, or about $46 billion. READ: Nvidia pauses AI cloud financing deals amid control, antitrust concerns (August 28, 2026)

historyItems.originalTitle: Chip-Machine Supplier ASML Boosts Guidance for Third Time on Surging AI Demand
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru ASML Holding improved its annual forecasts for the third time this year and said it was looking at ways to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines even more as the race to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuels demand for advanced chips. The Dutch group is projecting annual sales between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros, equivalent to a range of $49.27 billion to $50.39 billion, compared with prior guidance of 43 billion euros to 45 billion euros. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched metric of pricing power and profitability--should come in at roughly 56%, compared with a previous guidance range of 54% to 56%. The revisions show how much ASML's fortunes have come to benefit from the build-out of data centers that turned chips into a red-hot commodity. Surging semiconductor demand means that ASML's clients like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics and Intel will need more of its machines so they can produce enough chips. ASML shares in Amsterdam gained more than 2% in European morning trading, consolidating ASML's lead as Europe's most valuable listed company. Its stock is up more than 80% over the past 12 months on a wave of investor fervor around AI and expectations that chips and semiconductor-making tools will remain in high demand for years to come. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," ASML Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet said. AI demand pushed up the cost of certain types of chips as companies hoard semiconductors to power data centers, leading to a supply squeeze. Micron Technology Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said last month that supplies of memory and storage chips would be much tighter in the coming years. In a bid to cash in on that tightness, ASML is seeking to increase production of its deep ultraviolet lithography tools as well as its more advanced extreme ultraviolet systems. In July, it had earmarked a 30% boost in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. However, Fouquet said it was becoming clear that wouldn't be enough to meet demand and that ASML was looking at ways to bolster capacity even more, especially for 2028 and beyond. Earlier this year, ASML executives alluded to the possibility of price increases, saying that a tight chip market gave ASML more negotiating power. Finance chief Roger Dassen said that while the company had now completed conversations with key customers, the effect of higher prices wouldn't show on 2026 figures. "It will start to become visible partly in the course of 2027. The full impact of that you will start to see in 2028 and beyond," he said. ASML posted sales of 11.66 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 7.52 billion euros a year earlier. historyItems.title: GlobalFoundries 在美日交易中獲得 210 億美元建廠資金
historyItems.summary: GlobalFoundries Inc 計劃在日本政府高達 210 億美元的支持下建造兩座新的晶片工廠，其中美國還持有該公司 4% 的股份。根據週三宣布的一項協議，GlobalFoundries 將在其位於紐約州北部的工廠運營由美國和日本共同擁有的工廠。這些設施的資金來自日本承諾向美國投資 5,500 億美元的資金。這些工廠將生產所謂的基本晶片，即用於車輛、工業設備和通訊設備的重要但不太複雜的半導體。
historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries Gets $21 Billion for Plants in US-Japan Deal
historyItems.originalSummary: GlobalFoundries Inc plans to build two new chip plants with the backing of as much as US$21 billion from the Japanese government, part of an arrangement that also includes the US taking a 4 percent stake in the company. Under an agreement announced on Wednesday, GlobalFoundries will operate factories at its site in upstate New York that are jointly owned by the US and Japan. The facilities will be funded with money from Japan’s pledge to invest US$550 billion in the US. The factories will make so-called essential chips, the vital yet less sophisticated semiconductors used in vehicles, industrial equipment and communications gear. Photo: John Carl D’Annibale, The Albany Times Union via AP The GlobalFoundries agreement is meant to boost American production of essential chips and reduce dependence on East Asian suppliers — addressing a national security concern for the US. Under a broader arrangement with GlobalFoundries, the US Department of Commerce will take a roughly 4 percent equity stake in the company, “further enabling the American public to share in GF’s growth.” GlobalFoundries will get to redirect funds from a previous US CHIPS and Science Act grant to invest in honing its manufacturing abilities. That includes advancing its work in fields such as silicon photonics, chip packaging and silicon germanium. In a separate statement, the US Department of Commerce said it was reallocating US$955 million in CHIPS Act incentives to go toward GlobalFoundries’ factory expansion and modernization. As part of the agreement, the company will devote US$5 billion to capital investments at its plants in New York and Vermont. The new Japan-linked factories will be operated in the same way that GlobalFoundries runs its current facilities, which serve customers such as Apple Inc and Japanese firms including Renesas Electronics Corp. Profits will be divided among the owners and GlobalFoundries, following an approach laid out in last year’s US trade deal with Japan. US President Donald Trump touted the accord on his Truth Social site, saying it would help revitalize America’s industrial base and create jobs.

historyItems.originalTitle: Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'
historyItems.originalSummary: Dell shares plunged 11% on Wednesday, leading a data center equipment sell-off on mounting concerns that enterprise AI spending will not justify the AI buildout. Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), Oracle and Super Micro also declined. Barclays analysts downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to the equivalent of hold from buy in a Wednesday report to clients. The analysts cited enterprise AI timing after significant stock gains. Barclays analysts said enterprise spending at Dell, HPE and NetApp had not shown a meaningful acceleration related to AI. The analysts instead attributed increased revenue to the global memory shortage. The analysts noted that infrastructure companies had passed higher memory prices on to customers. Barclays analysts said businesses typically allocate just 5% of IT budgets to AI, despite growing expectations that enterprise AI adoption will drive hardware replacement. The analysts found that only about a quarter of total enterprise AI spending goes toward hardware. The analysts said normalizing and eventually declining memory prices could weigh on infrastructure-related revenue. Data center server and other backend equipment makers have attracted investor interest this year on expectations of large equipment sales linked to AI demand for years ahead. Dell shares have risen more than 300% this year, making Dell one of the market's top performers. HPE shares have risen about 160% this year. NetApp shares have doubled this year. However, sentiment toward AI infrastructure has shifted recently, partly because of concerning revenue figures from OpenAI. Investors also fear that rising interest rates will create difficulties because much of the AI buildout relies on debt. Oracle, a heavy borrower, fell 9% on Wednesday and is now down 33% for the year. Neocloud company CoreWeave plunged 15% on Wednesday, erasing CoreWeave's gains for 2026. Memory is a highly cyclical business. Memory stocks fell this week after China's ChangXin Memory Technologies, also known as CXMT, reported progress over the weekend on a new chip structure. Micron shares are down 11% for the week. South Korea's SK Hynix has fallen 13% in U.S. trading this week. Western Digital has dropped more than 8% this week.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to open 2 new chip plants in New York with $21 billion in financing from Japan
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.summary: 2026 年 10 月 15 日——根據美日倡議，格羅方德被選為計劃在其馬耳他和紐約製造基地建設的兩座新半導體工廠的技術提供商和運營商，該計劃可能提供高達 210 億美元的資金。該計畫將顯著擴大美國半導體製造能力，同時加強美國和日本在具有重要戰略意義的晶片技術方面的合作。預計初期投資約 100 億美元，將加速 GlobalFoundries 馬耳他園區首座新 300 毫米晶圓廠的建設。
historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries picked for two new Malta chip fabs in $21B U.S.-Japan investment push
historyItems.originalSummary: Oct-15th-2026– GlobalFoundries has been selected as the technology provider and operator for two new semiconductor fabs planned at its Malta, New York manufacturing site under a U.S.-Japan initiative that could provide up to $21 billion in funding. The program would significantly expand U.S. semiconductor manufacturing capacity while strengthening cooperation between the United States and Japan in strategically important chip technologies. An initial investment of approximately $10 billion is expected to accelerate construction of the first new 300mm fab at GlobalFoundries’ Malta campus. Groundbreaking is expected later this year, with the fab targeted to begin operations in 2029 . Once fully operational, the first facility is expected to add approximately 900,000 300mm wafers per year of U.S. manufacturing capacity. A further investment of approximately $10 billion could support construction of a second fab at the same site. If completed, the second facility would add roughly another 900,000 wafers of annual capacity. Under the initiative, Japan will provide the investment while GlobalFoundries will contribute its semiconductor technologies, manufacturing expertise and operational capabilities. GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen described the project as a new model for semiconductor manufacturing cooperation between the U.S. and Japan. “This is a bold new initiative for semiconductor manufacturing, bringing together the United States and Japan with GF’s differentiated technology and decades of manufacturing expertise to accelerate trusted capacity in New York.” The scale of the project would make it one of the most significant additions to U.S. semiconductor capacity in recent years. In parallel, GlobalFoundries has agreed with the U.S. Department of Commerce to amend its existing CHIPS and Science Act award.

historyItems.originalTitle: GlobalFoundries to Build Two Chip Plants With Up to $21 Billion Funding
historyItems.originalSummary: MALTA, N.Y. — Computer chip company GlobalFoundries Inc. said Wednesday it plans to open two factories in Malta, New York, financed by an investment of up to US$21 billion from Japan. The company said the deal was made possible by the Trump administration’s trade and investment agreement with the Japanese government. It said the initiative will accelerate semiconductor manufacturing in the U.S. and strengthen critical supply chains. The company previously received some federal funding to expand as part of a Biden administration program to expand chip production. As a result of the investment from Japan, that federal funding will now go to investments in other areas to advance semiconductor manufacturing, GlobalFoundries spokesperson Kenneth Craig said in an email. U.S. President Donald Trump posted on social media that the U.S. government will receive shares in GlobalFoundries, just as it did for Intel Corp., in an expansion of the administration’s policy of taking ownership stakes in private companies. GlobalFoundries said in a statement that roughly US$10 billion would accelerate construction of a chip factory to open in 2029 and the other US$10 billion would fund a second plant. Demand for semiconductors has surged in recent years thanks to artificial intelligence and the need for computing power at data centers. In July, Taiwan computer chipmaker TSMC said it plans to spend another US$100 billion on expanding its manufacturing capacity in the U.S. TSMC has been expanding chip fabrication plants in the U.S., Japan and Taiwan.

historyItems.originalTitle: Palantir and London mayor's office settle lawsuit over UK police contract
historyItems.originalSummary: In the United Kingdom, US technology company Palantir and the office of London Mayor Sadiq Khan have settled the company’s lawsuit over the decision not to approve a contract with London police worth £50 million, or $66 million. Channel NewsAsia reports , citing a joint statement by the parties. Palantir agreed with London police on a two-year contract to use artificial intelligence systems. They were intended to automate some tasks and help analyse evidence. However, London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime refused to approve the agreement. It told police that no open competition had been held for the contract. Reports said that Khan’s representative also expressed concerns that Palantir did not align with London’s values. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . In a joint statement, Palantir and London’s Mayor’s Office for Policing and Crime said they had settled the case and withdrawn their mutual allegations. The parties also said that the decision not to enter into the contract was not based on Palantir’s values or ethics, or on broader coverage of the company’s activities. The office said it does not and has never had a policy of refusing to enter into contracts with Palantir. The company may participate in future procurement procedures. The United Kingdom is also reviewing the National Health Service’s £330 million contract with Palantir. A parliamentary committee said there was a clear mismatch between the company and the United Kingdom’s values and recommended invoking an early termination clause. Louis Mosley, head of Palantir’s UK division, called the recommendation irresponsible.

historyItems.summary: 荷蘭阿姆斯特丹：對先進晶片製造設備的需求將持續數年，ASML 表示，隨著人工智慧投資熱潮繼續推動半導體擴張，客戶已經在尋求 2029 年甚至 2030 年的訂單。這家荷蘭公司是全球最大的用於生產人工智慧晶片和先進半導體的設備製造商，該公司10月14日表示，計劃在2027年和2028年增加的產能不足以滿足需求。 ASML 7 月表示，計劃在 2027 年將產能增加 30%，在 2028 年再增加 30%。執行長 Christophe Fouquet 表示，該公司目前看到「2028 年有大量訂單」。
historyItems.originalTitle: ASML's strong orders ease fears AI spending boom is running out of steam
historyItems.originalSummary: AMSTERDAM, Netherlands: Demand for advanced chipmaking equipment is stretching years into the future, with ASML saying customers are already looking to place orders for 2029 and even 2030 as the artificial intelligence investment boom continues to drive semiconductor expansion. The Dutch company, the world's biggest maker of equipment used to produce AI chips and advanced semiconductors, said October 14 that planned increases in its production capacity for 2027 and 2028 would not be enough to meet demand. ASML said in July that it planned to increase capacity by 30 percent in 2027 and by another 30 percent in 2028. CEO Christophe Fouquet said that the company was now seeing "a lot of order intake for 2028. But also, some strong interest to already place orders for 2029 and sometimes even 2030." The outlook helped ease investor concerns that the surge in spending on AI infrastructure could be approaching a peak. ASML's customers include TSMC, which manufactures chips for Nvidia, as well as Samsung, Intel, SK Hynix and Micron. The companies have been investing heavily to expand chip production. "There were concerns that the AI trade was running out of steam," said Gordon Kerr, European macro strategist at KBRA, adding ASML's results showed "demand for chips remains strong, and infrastructure spending is likely to continue well into 2027". ASML shares rose two percent on October 14. The stock has gained almost 70 percent this year, while the company is Europe's largest by market value at about €586 billion. The company reported third-quarter net profit of 4.96 billion euros on net sales of 11.7 billion euros. It forecast fourth-quarter sales of between 14.2 billion euros and 15.2 billion euros, or US$15.9 billion to $17 billion. ASML also raised its full-year sales outlook from at least 43 billion euros to 44 billion euros to 45 billion euros.

historyItems.originalTitle: Credo Launches Micro-Emitter Standardization Initiative | Business | Oct 2026
historyItems.originalSummary: Credo Launches Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Standardization for AI Data Center Scale-Up and Scale-Out Applications Joined by Initial Participants Including Leading Hyperscaler and Optical Technology Solution Providers AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC Under the OCP Networking Project Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd (Credo) (NASDAQ: CRDO), an innovator in providing connectivity at scale through fast, reliable, and energy-efficient system solutions, alongside prominent optical technology providers, today announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. Among the first to join with Credo include a leading hyperscaler as well as AFL, ams OSRAM, BizLink, Foxlink, Heraeus Covantics, SENKO, and YOFC, bringing together expertise spanning the full optical connectivity stack to advance the development of the wide, parallel optical connectivity ecosystem. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261012753816/en/ Credo, alongside prominent optical technology providers, has announced the launch of the Short-Reach Micro-Emitter Optics (SRMO) Workstream dedicated to developing a specification within the Open Compute Project (OCP) Community that will define a new class of high-speed data center interconnects. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. Micro-emitter technology brings new ways of moving volumes of data, while dramatically improving reliability, power efficiency, and bandwidth density. Arrays of micron-scale light sources make up the transmit side of an optical link. Rather than pushing a few optical channels to extreme data rates, many micro-emitters operate in parallel at optimal individual speeds, enabling layer zero redundancy to improve reliability. The SRMO Workstream was initiated to address the need for interoperable interconnects as wide, parallel micro-emitter technology drives new form factors across rapidly evolving scale-up and scale-out fabrics in AI data centers. The specification, targeted for OCP approval in 2027, will address requirements for link power, efficiency, signaling, parallelism, physical form factors – including module and connector footprint, link budget, and compliance. By defining specifications, the SRMO Workstream aims to give data center operators, hyperscalers, and system designers access to a broad ecosystem of interoperable components with supply chain resiliency, accelerating time to deployment and fostering continued innovation in optical connectivity. “As AI workloads scale from thousands to tens of thousands of accelerators, the industry needs a standardized approach to wide, parallel optical connectivity — not a patchwork of components that do not fit together or interoperate,” said L.K. historyItems.originalTitle: Department of Commerce Announces Agreement with GlobalFoundries to Amend Its Existing CHIPS Program Award and Reallocate $955 Million to Accelerate Investments in Silicon Photonics, Silicon-Germanium, and Advanced Packaging
historyItems.originalSummary: Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Office has agreed with GlobalFoundries to amend its existing award and reallocate up to $955 million in incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act. The amendment will increase the portion of an existing CHIPS Program award allocated to GlobalFoundries’ modernization and expansion of its semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Malta, NY and Burlington, VT. As part of the amendment, GlobalFoundries has agreed to expand its capital investment in these facilities to $5 billion. The total amount of the existing CHIPS Program award will not be increased. The investment will expand domestic manufacturing capacity for technologies increasingly critical to communications infrastructure and data centers, including silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies. “GlobalFoundries is expanding its investment to develop and manufacture critical semiconductor technologies enabling data center and high-performance compute infrastructure,” said Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director for Semiconductor Innovation and Investment at the Department of Commerce. “The CHIPS Program award supports GlobalFoundries efforts to onshore and accelerate the development of these important semiconductor components." GlobalFoundries is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling technologies from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GlobalFoundries delivers differentiated, power efficient, and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high growth markets. historyItems.originalTitle: Flex Completes Acquisition of EPC Power, Expanding Power Conversion Capabilities for AI Data Centers and Grid Applications
historyItems.originalSummary: AUSTIN, Texas , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Flex (NASDAQ: FLEX) announced that it has completed its acquisition of EPC Power, a leading provider of intelligent power conversion solutions for data center and grid applications. EPC Power is now part of Flex’s Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, expanding the company’s capabilities across power, cooling and compute to address growing demand for higher-density AI infrastructure and next-generation 800V data center power architectures. “We are pleased to welcome the EPC Power team to Flex,” said Revathi Advaithi, Chief Executive Officer of Flex. “EPC Power adds differentiated power conversion and grid-forming technology to our capabilities across power, cooling and compute. Together, we can help customers address the growing power demands of AI infrastructure with more efficient, resilient and integrated solutions.” EPC Power combines proprietary hardware, software and controls with U.S.-based engineering and manufacturing. With more than 15 GW deployed, its technology supports grid stabilization and backup power, and its platform is engineered to support next generation 800V data center power architectures. Flex plans to separate its Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment into an independent publicly traded company, Axiom Solutions International, Inc., in the first calendar quarter of 2027.

historyItems.originalSummary: Amkor Technology, Inc. (Nasdaq: AMKR), a leading provider of outsourced semiconductor packaging and test services, today announced additional investments in South Korea for capacity expansion initiatives with NVIDIA. With this latest commitment, Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea total $3 billion. The initiatives support growing demand for next-generation AI and accelerated computing platforms.Advanced packaging technologies are essential to enabling the performance, power efficiency and integration required for next-generation computing systems. The prepayments align Amkor's manufacturing capacity with NVIDIA’s long-term growth plans and support increasing demand for advanced packaging solutions.“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel, president and chief executive officer of Amkor Technology. “These investments build on our global manufacturing footprint and strengthen our ability to support customers through our operations in both the United States and South Korea.”“Growing demand for accelerated computing is increasing the need for advanced packaging capacity,” said Debora Shoquist, executive vice president, operations of NVIDIA. “Our work with Amkor helps us scale production of current and next-generation platforms while strengthening the resilience of our global supply chain.”This collaboration further strengthens Amkor’s role as a strategic manufacturing partner for NVIDIA and reinforces the companies’ shared commitment to supporting the continued expansion of AI infrastructure.Amkor will also exhibit at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. from Nov. 30 - Dec. 3, where the company will showcase its advanced packaging and test capabilities and engage with customers, policymakers and industry leaders.About Amkor Technology, Inc.Amkor Technology, Inc. The company’s comprehensive portfolio includes advanced packaging, wafer-level processing, and system-in-package solutions targeting applications for smartphones, data centers, artificial intelligence, automobiles and wearables. historyItems.originalTitle: Coherent (COHR) Stock Looks About Right Following Sold Out Capacity News
historyItems.originalSummary: Coherent has become one of the most prominent optical hardware stories in the market. After a very steep multi year climb, the key question is whether the current share price lines up with what its earnings can reasonably support. Over the past 3 years the stock has returned about 7x, which places significant emphasis on the idea that its profit power can eventually catch up with that move. Recent headlines around sold out optical capacity into 2029 and tighter supply for certain data center components may support expectations for stronger earnings and cash generation over time, but they also raise the stakes if those hopes do not materialize. Your read on Coherent is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Coherent's shares could be worth .

historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile 合作夥伴 Ligado 敦促 FCC 仔細審查 Rocket Lab 提出的 80 億美元收購 Iridium 的提議。 Ligado 援引了 SpaceX 的指控，稱 Iridium 在八個月內提交了 50 多份拒絕申請。 Neutron 的首次亮相已推遲到 2027 年，而 Iridium 收購仍計劃在 2027 年中期完成。 Rocket Lab (RKLB) 的股價上週暴跌超過 25%，因為其上市計畫再次被推遲。 Neutron 火箭對該股造成重創，而 AST SpaceMobile 的頻譜合作夥伴 Ligado Networks 對其提議以 80 億美元收購 Iridium Communications 的競爭優勢提出質疑。 RKLB 股票週五收在 50.84 美元，當日下跌近 8%。

The decline extended its losing streak to eight sessions, wiping out 38% of its value since its Oct.7 close. The selloff deepened after Rocket Lab pushed Neutron’s debut into 2027. Ligado Takes Aim At Iridium DealIn a recent letter to the FCC, Ligado accused Iridium of using regulatory proceedings to delay competing satellite services, including Ligado’s proposed SkyTerra Next offering with AST SpaceMobile.Iridium has long used the FCC’s procedures as an anticompetitive weapon,” Ligado’s lawyers said.“While Rocket Lab and Iridium tout MSS competition as the core public interest benefit of the acquisition, Iridium’s own conduct suggests its modus operandi at the FCC for decades has been to suppress rather than promote competition,” Ligado said.Ligado asked the FCC to scrutinize the transaction’s incentives and public-interest benefits, particularly if Iridium does not withdraw filings that Ligado characterizes as attempts to cause delay.AST SpaceMobile Plans Fuel Spectrum FightLigado’s commercial interest runs directly through SkyTerra Next, a proposed mobile satellite service using AST SpaceMobile’s low-Earth-orbit constellation to support direct-to-device connectivity.Ligado alleges that Iridium has opposed the service to protect its existing business. It argues that SkyTerra Next would compete with Iridium without creating an interference risk. The letter also points to Iridium’s previous interest in accessing Ligado’s spectrum. According to Ligado, the FCC rejected the move, after which Iridium continued pursuing objections concerning potential interference. Ligado said that the acquisition could reinforce those incentives by increasing the importance of protecting the strategic value of Iridium’s L-band spectrum.“Accordingly, we urge the Commission to carefully scrutinize the transaction to ensure that the parties’ intent and incentives align with the public interest,” its lawyers said.SpaceX’s Objections Enter Deal FightLigado also drew on SpaceX’s earlier criticism of Iridium, citing an August filing accusing the operator of repeatedly attempting to impede competitors. “Iridium exploits Commission procedure to deny or delay its competitors from providing better service to millions of American consumers, businesses, and first responders,” SpaceX said in the filing quoted by Ligado.According to Ligado’s letter, SpaceX documented more than 50 petitions to deny filed by Iridium over an eight-month period. historyItems.originalTitle: Oracle Proposes Plan that could deliver at least $155M to offset customers utility costs in New Mexico
historyItems.originalSummary: Austin, Texas-Oct 13, 2026 Oracle today announced a proposed Energy Service Agreement with El Paso Electric (EPE) for Project Jupiter to support late-stage construction, initial commissioning, emergency backup power at the site and to meet life safety needs for New Mexican workers at the data center. As indicated earlier this year, the primary power source for Project Jupiter will continue to be provided by the Bloom Energy fuel cell microgrid. There is no change to our plan. As part of the Energy Service Agreement, Oracle expects to pay $10 million for power annually for 10 years even if its usage is below contracted levels. This agreement helps offset shared electric system costs that would otherwise be borne by EPE's New Mexico customers and supports affordable electric rates. In addition, a separate agreement includes a proposal to provide as much as $55 million annually in direct credits for up to three years for EPE's New Mexico residential and small business customers. This credit could begin benefiting customers in 2027. "We welcome the opportunity to facilitate Oracle's credit to further affordability for our customers," said Kelly Tomblin, president and CEO of El Paso Electric. "Growth and investment in New Mexico has always been an EPE priority and we support the effort Oracle is making to ensure that this growth benefits our residential and small commercial customers." Earlier this year, Oracle signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge and made a commitment to pays its own way for energy and infrastructure costs. The proposed agreements with El Paso Electric not only ensure that Oracle pays for the energy costs, but it also supports affordable rates and additional offset of energy costs for its neighbors. "We realize the impact that electric rate increases have on the community and our proposed solution takes that burden off of New Mexico ratepayers," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, executive vice president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. "We're taking this action now - well before our data center comes online - to deliver a direct, meaningful benefit to New Mexico households and small businesses and help ensure the community shares in the value created by Project Jupiter." Additional information will be provided following the filing of the Energy Service Agreement. historyItems.originalTitle: Is Applied Materials (AMAT) A Bargain Following Its EPIC Center Launch?

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Lifts Off for Thursday Cargo Delivery
historyItems.originalSummary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station. Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS. The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Counts Down to Launch for Station Resupply Mission
historyItems.originalSummary: HOUSTON (CW39) — NASA’s SpaceX resupply mission aboard a Dragon spacecraft docked with the International Space Station on Thursday. The Dragon spacecraft, which launched from Cape Canaveral on Tuesday aboard a Falcon 9 rocket, is carrying more than 6,300 pounds of supplies and hardware for the ISS, including new scientific experiments, cargo, and the final pair of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays to the orbiting laboratory. The final pair of solar arrays will complete the space station’s power system augmentation, boosting available electricity for research, operations, and the station’s safe, controlled deorbit. Astronauts will install the arrays during a series of spacewalks planned for later this fall. The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.

historyItems.title: 如何投資 SpaceX (SPCX)——以及如何不投資
historyItems.summary: 太空探索技術公司正在透過新的環境影響報告計畫尋求美國聯邦航空管理局的批准，以將博卡奇卡的星艦活動從目前的 25 次發射提高到每年 456 次發射和 912 次著陸的潛在上限，同時在全球範圍內擴大星艦著陸和支出地點。同一時期，SpaceX 承諾斥資近 80 億美元購買 800 MHz 行動頻譜，並已獲得 FCC 許可，可發射多達 15,000 顆直接連接手機的 Starlink 衛星，這使得該公司成為資本密集的全球營運商和高節奏發射營運商。現在的焦點轉移到太空探索科技公司的投資敘事如何融入資本密集的星鏈移動和星艦擴張。
historyItems.originalTitle: How to Invest In SpaceX (SPCX) — And How Not To
historyItems.originalSummary: Space Exploration Technologies is seeking FAA approval, via a new Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement, to lift Starship activity at Boca Chica from the current 25 launches to a potential ceiling of 456 launches and 912 landings a year, while scaling Starship landing and expenditure sites globally. In the same period, SpaceX has committed nearly US$8b to acquire 800 MHz of mobile spectrum and has secured FCC clearance for up to 15,000 direct-to-cellphone Starlink satellites, which moves the business toward a capital-intensive role as both global carrier and high-cadence launch operator. The focus now shifts to how Space Exploration Technologies' investment narrative incorporates this capital-heavy Starlink Mobile and Starship expansion.
